sources.note: Gives each retrieval step of a search agent a dense reward built from two ground-truth-conditioned signals — how much the step raised the model's likelihood of the correct answer, and how necessary the step looks in hindsight — and fuses them asymmetrically so that a step which helps locally but is redundant globally is discounted.
sources.title: BiCAA: Bidirectional Credit Assignment for Search-Augmented Agent

sources.note: Re-scores a search agent's own sampled tokens under a teacher that has been shown the instance's supporting evidence, and uses the detached teacher-student gap to nudge the GRPO advantage up or down on search and answer tokens only, without adding a distillation loss or changing anything at inference.
sources.title: EviSD: Evidence-Conditioned Self-Distillation for Search-Augmented Agents

sources.note: Supervises audio reasoning with per-question rubrics generated from the raw waveform, and keeps the signal alive as the policy improves by regenerating the rubrics from the model's own rollouts each step and pruning any criterion that every rollout satisfies or none does.
sources.title: Reinforcement Learning with Evolving Rubrics as Rewards for Audio Reasoning

sources.note: Scores each reasoning step of a translation by how much appending it raises a frozen reference model's teacher-forced likelihood of the gold translation, and adds that as a dense per-step reward on top of sequence-level quality — after first establishing that explicit reasoning helps long and hard inputs while drifting on terminology and style.
sources.title: PAMT: Process-Aligned Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Domain Machine Translation

sources.note: Diagnoses label-free RLVR's collapse as a shortcut in which the same answer-level consensus signal both estimates the reward and receives the gradient, and fixes it by masking the answer span from updates entirely — so a reward can only be raised by improving the reasoning that produces the answer.
sources.title: Don't Peek at the Answer: Outcome-Masked Group Relative Policy Optimization for Label-Free RLVR

sources.note: Assigns credit in coding-agent RL by splitting each code diff into sub-diffs, matching semantically similar sub-diffs across rollouts to form advantage groups, and projecting the resulting diff-level advantage back onto the tokens that produced it.
sources.title: DiDPO: Diff-in-Diff Policy Optimization for Coding Agent Training

sources.note: Distributes hindsight supervision across the turns of an agent trajectory by comparing each turn's share of total revision magnitude against its share of eligible tokens, holding the average multiplier at one so the total supervision is fixed and only its allocation changes -- and isolates that allocation with a permutation control that keeps the multiplier values and scrambles which turn receives which.
sources.title: Trajectory-Relative Hindsight Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

sources.note: Replaces the monotonic zoom-in that tool-using video agents follow once they pick a region with a policy that self-checks each tool observation and can switch regions, and trains it with turn-level credit applied multiplicatively -- reweighting the trajectory advantage's magnitude while preserving its sign -- rather than additively.
sources.title: SCOUT: Self-Checking and Recovery-Aware Tool-Thought Agents for Ultra-Long Egocentric Video Reasoning

sources.note: Trains a multimodal agent to orchestrate twelve video-analysis tools for anomaly detection with GRPO under a dual reward that combines exact-match rule checks with an LLM judge scoring logicality, relevance and completeness, and releases the benchmark it is evaluated on.
sources.title: VTO: Visual Tool Orchestration for Video Anomaly Detection

sources.note: Builds a dense process reward without a learned verifier or an online judge, by aligning generated reasoning steps to the process-labelled reference steps that existing datasets already contain using numerical, symbolic and lexical matching rules, gated so a partial reference match cannot override a wrong final answer.
sources.title: StructReward: Efficient Structured Process Rewards for Self-Correcting Multimodal Reasoning

sources.note: Replaces the single tolerance threshold that RLVR uses to score floating-point answers with a hybrid reward pairing a hard clinical-safety constraint against a continuous precision-sensitive term, and adds a reward for stating the computational formula explicitly so an external verifier can check it.
sources.title: MedCalc-R1: Knowledge-Guided Reward Framework for Medical Mathematical Reasoning

sources.note: Traces the brittleness of multimodal RLVR gains under paraphrase and template change to two properties of the standard objective -- a binary verifier that cannot distinguish a wrong answer from a misformatted one, and a training distribution covering a thin slice of the prompts a deployed model meets -- and fixes both with a trinary reward and an invariance penalty across semantically equivalent prompts.
sources.title: Improving Generalization Robustness of Multimodal RLVR

sources.note: Shows on four internal Netflix verification tasks that explicit reasoning usually degrades subjective judgement, that applying RLVR to fix it makes the policy abandon deliberation for short heuristic guessing, and that a length bonus gated on answer correctness is what stops the collapse.
sources.title: LLM Reasoning for Subjective Tasks: Failure Modes, Mitigation, and Dynamic Reasoning Routing

sources.note: Tests whether systems that translate natural-language reasoning steps into Lean preserve invalidity as well as validity, by automatically perturbing steps to make them wrong, and finds pervasive silent correction -- with the systems best at preserving valid inputs the most likely to repair invalid ones.
sources.title: FaithformBench: Benchmarking Faithfulness of Mathematical Chain-of-Thought Autoformalisation

sources.note: Trains an open-weight model with GRPO against a safety-gated LLM-as-a-judge rubric for financial advice, then audits the result with a judge-independent causal estimator on logged outcomes -- and finds the two evaluations rank the other systems differently, with the untrained base model last on the rubric and second on the audit.
sources.title: GRPO for Financial Advice Generation: Outperforming Commercial LLMs under CATE Evaluation

sources.note: Gives a search agent an explicitly reversible trajectory tree with reflect and backtrack as first-class actions, and trains the reflection policy with a dense local signal distilled from a teacher that can see the whole trajectory alongside the sparse terminal reward the local decision is ultimately judged by.
sources.title: LoongReflect: Boosting Long-Horizon Reflection in Search Agents via Global Perspective Distillation

sources.note: Splits a spatial-reasoning chain of thought into explicitly typed segments -- perception, including depth, and reasoning -- and gives each its own process reward and its own advantage term, so that the two do not compete for credit under a single outcome signal.
sources.title: SCOUT: Unlocking Enhanced Spatial Reasoning via Structured Chain-of-Thought and Multi-Objective Process Reward

sources.note: Formalizes 'spend test-time compute well' as a meta-reinforcement-learning problem — treating one long output stream as a sequence of episodes and scoring it by cumulative regret over tokens — and trains against a dense progress bonus that outcome-only reward cannot express.
sources.title: Optimizing Test-Time Compute via Meta Reinforcement Fine-Tuning

Name those. Leave the list empty rather than repeating what the sources already put side by side.

Rules:

- Ground every statement in the supplied material. If something is not stated,
  leave the field empty rather than inferring it.

aliases: string - other names the sources use for the same thing
output_schema.definition: string - two to four sentences defining the entity as the cited sources use it, not as a textbook would
output_schema.kind: string - one of: concept, method, dataset, model
related: string - name of a neighbouring entity worth linking to. Kept as you give it and never derived away, so name what a reader should turn to next rather than what happens to appear alongside this. Answering again replaces the whole list; an empty list retracts

result.definition: Scoring a whole trajectory by whether its final answer is correct, which collapses everything the model did into one bit. Across 18 sources it is the cheap, load-bearing signal that nothing has been able to replace. The complaint is uniform: a ten-retrieval search trajectory receives one scalar and nothing distinguishes the retrieval that found the key document from one that repeated a query; the reward supervises only the answer, so a model can reach it without attending to the audio, the image or the intermediate quantities at all; and over a long tool-use trajectory it supplies no supervision at the exact point where credit is most ambiguous. Yet every source that ablates it finds it indispensable rather than merely helpful, and the archive holds no instance of dense supervision anchoring a policy on its own -- removing the terminal reward is repeatedly the largest single loss, and one system with it removed keeps perfect step-level tool selection while never terminating. The design consequence the sources converge on is that dense signals should be applied as modifiers that cannot flip a sign or create an update where the outcome reward is silent: one applies its turn-level term multiplicatively rather than additively for exactly this reason, another gates partial reference agreement so it cannot override a wrong final answer, and a third bounds a privileged correction by the magnitude of the outcome advantage. A separate limitation is that its scope is the answer: post-training against it improves solution accuracy without necessarily improving the semantic validity of the traces, which one source notes should be unsurprising given what it scores.
